vocab.notes: Jak vypadá? What does he/she look like?
Spíš menší (rather short) is the polite way to say it.
Plural only: Má brýle. Nosí brýle.

dialogue.setting: Daniel's first week. He needs to give something to Pavel from IT, but doesn't know who he is.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.cs: Promiň, nevíš, kdo je Pavel z IT? Mám mu něco předat.
lines.en: Sorry, do you know who Pavel from IT is? I need to give him something.

lines.speaker: Jana
lines.cs: Pavel? Je vysoký, má krátké tmavé [[vlasy|vlas|acc.pl|object]] a [[brýle|brýle|acc.pl|object]].
lines.en: Pavel? He's tall, with short dark hair and glasses.

spoken.form: Je vysokej, má krátký tmavý vlasy a brýle.
spoken.note: -ej for -ý (vysokej), and -ý for the plural -é (krátký tmavý vlasy).

lines.speaker: Jana
lines.cs: Ne, nemá. Dnes má modrou [[košili|košile|acc|object]]. Sedí tamhle u [[okna|okno|gen|after-u]].
lines.en: No, he doesn't. Today he's wearing a blue shirt. He sits over there by the window.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.en: Oh, I can see him now. Thanks!

exercises.listen: Je vysoký, má krátké tmavé vlasy a brýle.
options: Short, long dark hair, a beard
Tall, short fair hair, no glasses

hints.wrong: Short, long dark hair, a beard
hints.explain: "Vysoký" is tall, "krátké" short (hair), and he has "brýle", glasses.

hints.wrong: Tall, short fair hair, no glasses
hints.explain: "Tmavé" is dark (fair would be "světlé"), and he does have "brýle".

exercises.why: "Je vysoký, má krátké tmavé vlasy a brýle." He's tall, with short dark hair and glasses.
"Dnes má modrou košili." Today he's wearing a blue shirt.

lines: Pavel je vysoký, má krátké tmavé vlasy a brýle. Dnes má modrou košili.

exercises.prompt: What colour is Pavel's shirt today?

hints.explain: "Tmavé" describes his hair. The shirt is "modrou", blue.
White would be "bílou". "Modrou košili" is a blue shirt.

exercises.why: "Dnes má modrou košili": today he's wearing a blue shirt.
See "Word order and the little words": new information goes last, and jsem, se, si, mi, ho… go second.
Adjectives agree with the noun they describe. manažerka is feminine, so vysoký → vysoká.

hints.explain: vysoký is the masculine form. manažerka is feminine: vysoká.
-é is for neuter nouns (or plurals). manažerka is feminine: vysoká.

exercises.why: vlasy is a masculine inanimate plural. Adjectives describing it end in -é, in both nominative and accusative: krátké vlasy.

hints.explain: vlasy is plural, so the adjective is plural too: krátké vlasy.
-í is the plural for people (masc. animate): milí kolegové. For vlasy it's -é: krátké vlasy.

exercises.why: brýle (glasses) only exists in the plural. Czech says "has glasses" (má brýle) or "wears glasses" (nosí brýle).

hints.explain: brýle is always plural, like English "glasses": Má brýle.

exercises.why: Jak vypadá? literally "How does he look?". Use jak, not co, and no se.

hints.explain: Jaký je? means "What's he like (as a person)?". For appearance: Jak vypadá?

exercises.why: See "Word order and the little words": new information goes last, and jsem, se, si, mi, ho… go second.

hints.explain: Ho is one of the little words: it goes second, not at the end. Už ho vidím.

answers: {He is|He's} tall and {has|he has|he's got|has got} dark hair[.]
exercises.why: vysoký = tall; má tmavé vlasy = (he) has dark hair.

exercises.question: Which case is "modrou"?
exercises.en: Today he's wearing a blue shirt.
exercises.why: košili is the object of má (has), so it's in the accusative, and the adjective agrees: modrá košile → modrou košili.

context.speaker: Kolega
context.en: What does your manager look like?

exercises.prompt: Say she's tall and has long hair.
exercises.why: Feminine adjective vysoká; vlasy is plural, so dlouhé vlasy.

hints.explain: Your manager is a woman here (manažerka): vysoká.
Standard Czech: dlouhé vlasy. (You will hear dlouhý vlasy in speech; see the note on spoken forms.)

exercises.why: mít: mám, máš, má, máme, máte, mají. For on/ona: má.

hints.explain: mám is "I have". For ona (my sister): má.
